decision.title: The Clothworkers Foundation — Small Grants Programme
why: funder has backed GB-CHC organisations (81% of awards)
gaps: Match funding requirement not explicitly confirmed in call brief (£6,000 reserves available but requires board sign-off)
How a refrigerated van will specifically expand the Food Pantry model or geographical reach (funding history lists it as needed, but does not explain the intended use or expansion mechanism)
Specific new capacity or member numbers expected from van addition
auditor could not ground: A refrigerated van will let us expand our Food Pantry model beyond our current 190 member households
decision.direction:
Lead with the freezer as the direct enabler of meal volume and consistency for your most food-insecure households in Peckham and Nunhead.

Your 2025-26 data shows exactly why: 7,400 meals served across 148 sittings with 74% of surveyed members (n=180) now eating a hot meal daily more often than before, and your food pantry members reporting an average £61 monthly reduction in food spend. The current 2016 freezer fails monthly—each breakdown directly interrupts this consistency. Your independent evaluation by Southwark Impact Partnership (June 2025) and twice-yearly beneficiary surveys (31% response rate since 2022) give the funder concrete evidence that replacement equipment translates into measurable outcomes for people facing financial hardship.

Avoid framing this as organisational need rather than beneficiary impact; the funder backs capital equipment *for buildings and services to disadvantaged communities*, not operational resilience alone. Do not mention the van in your lead narrative—it diffuses the case and raises complexity around match funding that you'll need board approval to confirm; keep the freezer as your single focused ask unless the funder's form explicitly invites multiple items.
decision.question: What difference will this funding make to the people you work with, and how will you know? Give us evidence from your existing work.
